evidence.note: Genuine design-level adaptation: tried formulas.ExcelModel, found it is file-based and doesn't fit a cell-referenced model, and pivoted to a custom engine reusing get_functions() implementations. A real course-correction on a falsified library assumption.

Correctly diagnosed the root cause of all-endpoints-timeout as a non-reentrant threading.Lock deadlock (patch_cells holds wb_lock then save_state re-acquires) plus a \\d+ regex-escaping bug. Root-cause identification of a falsified assumption, but it's a concurrency/tooling crash, not an Excel/spill/recompute semantic assumption.

For ~150 steps the agent repeats the identical Lock->RLock + regex patch, restarts, re-runs tests, but never confirms the fix landed or achieves green — near-verbatim repeated analysis. Failure to detect that its correction approach itself is not progressing; no re-verification loop closes.

Server reached 2558 lines with full engine/endpoints, but the trajectory never advanced past the deadlock to exercise Excel edge cases, spill, topological order, or perf budgets — so no adaptation on the semantic assumptions the dimension targets ever occurred.

reasoning: The agent shows one authentic early design pivot (ExcelModel to custom engine) and a correct root-cause diagnosis of a deadlock, which lifts it above 'ignores contradicting evidence.' But the dominant, whole-horizon behavior matches anchor 3: it reacts to a hard crash with a local patch (RLock/regex) and never revisits or re-verifies, getting trapped in a ~150-step non-progressing loop that repeats the same fix. It never reached the Excel/spill/recompute/perf assumptions this dimension centers on, so there is no evidence of reworking a semantic design (anchor 8) — placing it at 3.
